proposal.name: Run configured Go acceptance tests with independent evidence

issue_plan.name: Run configured Go acceptance tests with independent evidence
issue_plan.summary: Three ordered plumbing changes add the shared offline acceptance lifecycle, implement Go selection and completion evidence, and connect that execution to planning and builder checks. Each selector must independently fail on the base and pass on the candidate, using its pinned source, identity and captured command authority; suite results and diagnostics cannot substitute for that evidence. The changes preserve the unconfigured Go runner, existing hashes and locks, offline isolation and shared deadlines, and keep other native frameworks and external repository intake disabled. SPEC.md, README.md and docs/factory.md will describe the completed behavior, and the merger records the execution decisions before moving to the next issue.

issues.title: Add the shared lifecycle for configured acceptance evidence
issues.body:
Implement the framework-independent execution and evidence foundation for #513, continuing #501's native-acceptance work within step 4 of #452's ratified plan. The existing captured execution API from #484 runs suite commands but stops at the first failure and returns diagnostics only. The native identity change in #503 pins sources, (part, framework, file, selector) identities and execution authority. This issue supplies the lower-level lifecycle needed to collect independent acceptance evidence; it does not yet enable a production framework adapter or lift the configured planning refusal.

Build on internal/plumbing/repository_checks.go, repository_docker.go and dependencies.go. Extend the trusted host/environment boundary so a framework invocation returns completion evidence separately from stdout/stderr diagnostics and from ordinary CommandResults. Keep the suite Run and Close behavior usable without an acceptance-capable environment. An environment lacking the required evidence capability must refuse acceptance explicitly, never reconstruct evidence from diagnostics. The trusted caller chooses adapters; a candidate, command output or IPC request cannot register one or supply replacement execution policy.

Before preparation, validate the captured snapshot, execution binding, ownership, supported invocation form and available adapter capability. Before executing acceptance, verify and stage the pinned source bytes with the existing safe-file and line-ending rules. Bind each host-issued invocation to a fresh invocation identity, the complete acceptance identity, package attribution when applicable, source bytes and captured configuration. Evidence must belong to that invocation and prove one unambiguous matching selection and its completion. Preserve both completed and unfinished identities, reasons and the distinction between completed test failure, attributable compiler failure, setup failure, skipped, refused, running and unstarted work. The adapter will supply framework-specific completion and compiler attribution in the next issue; the shared layer must not invent either.

Validate records defensively. Missing selections, duplicate matches or terminals, contradictory or truncated records, stale invocation records, wrong part/framework/file/selector/package/source/configuration, and nonzero exit without attributable evidence cannot become completed acceptance failures or passes. Exit zero, suite success, the legacy Accepted map, textual PASS/FAIL, JSON printed by a workload and runner-looking markers are never evidence. Preserve diagnostics for explanation without parsing them into authoritative records. Summary and structured-result handling must retain failed and unfinished full identities and reasons even when output is clipped.

Provide distinct internal base-check and candidate-check paths sharing this lifecycle. A base run must attempt independent selectors after expected ordinary test or compile failures while its environment remains usable; it cannot simply call the existing first-failure suite loop. Never turn a format, lint, install, tool-launch, discovery or unrelated setup error into acceptance evidence. The base verdict requires a completed attributable failure for every selector, and any selector already passing invalidates it. A candidate verdict requires every applicable configured command and every acceptance selector to pass. Ordinary command failures remain failures even when acceptance passes. Failed preparation, startup or cleanup, cancellation, interrupted execution and any exhausted allowance veto draft qualification even after an earlier completed failure. Retain the results already obtained and explicit unfinished results for the rest.

Use the existing DependencyPreparer and verified immutable environments. Preserve captured command argument boundaries and reasons for inapplicable phases, part ownership, source staging, root-owned container copies, offline checks with no pulls/downloads/installations, explicit environment, overridden entrypoint, proxy suppression, init, 4 GiB memory, 1,024 processes and no host cache mounts. Keep at most one candidate environment active per admitted check. Parts retain their disposable build outputs; every active environment is closed before another opens. Adapter work must not add Python as a runtime requirement to Go or Node images.

All work in one run shares the original whole-run deadline, at most twelve minutes and any shorter caller/preparer allowance, including selection, preparation, staging, startup, suite work and acceptance. Start one test-phase allowance of at most ten minutes at the first suite or acceptance test-phase work; later invocations and parts consume what remains. Neither allowance renews. Preserve the existing startup reserve and bounded fifteen-second cleanup with an uncanceled context, cleanup of partial startup, and queue ownership until cleanup finishes. Returning a completed test failure must not bypass checking cancellation or cleanup errors.

Add default Go acceptance/regression coverage using trusted fake adapters and environments, with no Docker or network. Exercise the lower-level lifecycle itself: two selectors with independent verdicts after a suite failure; success requiring all commands and selectors; mixed passing/failing base results; unavailable adapter/evidence capability; missing, duplicate, conflicting, truncated, stale and mismatched evidence; stdout/stderr forgery; clipped diagnostics; later-part deadlines and cancellation after earlier failure; preparation/startup/cleanup errors; one active environment; and uncanceled bounded cleanup while the queue remains owned. The test seam belongs to trusted host code, not candidate configuration. Retain the existing acceptance suite and unconfigured Go behavior.

Update SPEC.md and docs/factory.md to describe the implemented lower-level interface and limits while stating that configured native admission still awaits integration. Keep README.md accurate and within 400 lines. Each changed SPEC bullet cites its foundations; no claim of runnable native acceptance is made yet. This plumbing build cannot write decisions/: the merger records this execution foundation before the next issue. Unavailable Docker/network verification and decision recording are Merger work, not repair findings; affected opt-in real Python and TLAPS CI suites remain required.

Foundations: D-0105, D-0107, D-0108, D-0110, D-0111, D-0121, D-0122, D-0173, D-0281, D-0282, D-0294, D-0301 and D-0305; #452's ratified plan; #484 and D-0311's captured execution API; #503 and D-0314's native identity contract. Preserve legacy plan hashes and locks. External repository intake stays disabled; pytest, Vitest and Jest remain explicitly unsupported.

Kind: plumbing

issues.title: Implement exact Go selection and independent completion evidence
issues.body:
Implement the Go adapter for #513 on the shared configured-acceptance lifecycle and evidence boundary delivered by the preceding issue. This continues #501 within #452's ratified plan, using #484's RepositoryChecks snapshot and verified dependency environments, and #503's pinned native identities. Deliver a working lower-level Go adapter and test it with real Go processes now. Keep configured factory admission disabled until the following integration issue connects planning, the builder tool and final checks.

Execute each Go acceptance selector separately through its owning part's captured test_one command, in that part's directory. The source bytes and (part, framework, file, selector) identity must be the pinned ones, bound to the captured execution digest. The adapter may constrain selection and attach trusted evidence collection; it must not replace the declared command with a different execution policy, enable network access, install tools or download dependencies.

Support safe direct go test templates with exactly one {test} placeholder as the value of -run or -run=, including both {test} and ^{test}$ forms. Support the documented form ["go", "test", "./...", "-run", "^{test}$", "-count=1"] by narrowing its package scope to the acceptance file's actual package within the owning part. Escape literal selector data using Go's regexp rules and anchor every Go slash-separated selector component, including exact subtest paths. Prefix matches, regex metacharacters, shell syntax, glob characters and option-looking data must remain literal identities. Select one package with its normal production files and dependencies, not a go test invocation over the acceptance file alone. Preserve applicable build tags and other declared execution policy. Refuse an explicit package scope that does not include the target, conflicting selection flags, repetitions or modes that cannot yield one completed selection, opaque commands whose semantics cannot be established, and any form that cannot be safely narrowed without changing policy. Never interpolate selector data into shell or interpreter source, including sh -c or equivalent templates. Unsupported forms fail explicitly before preparation/execution rather than falling back to another command. Document the actual supported forms and reasons for refusal.

Establish the selected package and confirm that the requested top-level function is the Go testing declaration in the ratified file, among the files actually selected by the toolchain and build constraints. Handle ordinary and external test packages correctly. Distinguish identical function names in other files, packages, modules and parts. Reject wrong-file declarations, excluded files, duplicates and multiple matches instead of accepting a similarly named function elsewhere. Exact subtest selection must be confirmed at runtime; running only its parent, siblings or a parameterized family is insufficient.

Collect Go testing lifecycle and terminal evidence through the trusted boundary, independently of diagnostic stdout/stderr. A process exit, a textual PASS/FAIL, test2json-looking JSON, synthetic process-exit failure or fabricated runner marker is not a substitute for the selected test's start and terminal completion. Validate the fresh invocation and complete identity supplied by the common lifecycle. Require exactly one matching completed selection; retain relevant parent/child lifecycle so a parent result cannot conceal an absent or unfinished requested subtest. Report selected skips explicitly and do not accept them as passes or base failures. Refuse zero-test success, exit without running tests, missing completion, duplicate or stale results, conflicting/truncated evidence and results from another file, package or part. Actual assertion and panic failures with completed framework failure evidence qualify as failed; abrupt exit or interrupted execution without that evidence does not.

Preserve the proposed-new-API workflow. A completed compiler failure may be eligible base evidence only when independently attributed to the selected acceptance package's use of the proposed API. Record that attribution separately from runtime test completion, for the selected invocation; do not broadcast a failing suite or another package's compiler result to unrelated acceptance identities. Missing Go/compiler tools, unresolved dependencies, broken package discovery, unrelated source/package failures and interrupted compilation cannot qualify. Fresh candidate execution must produce actual passing tests once the API is implemented; a successful compile alone is never a pass. Compilation, discovery, evidence collection and execution consume the common run and test-phase budgets and cannot reset them.

Add default Go tests with small standard-library-only modules and real Go compilation/testing, without Docker or network. Use the production selection and evidence code, not a fake JSON producer standing in for Go. Required cases include: a test failing against base code and passing after only production changes with identical acceptance bytes; two tests in one package where one already passes and the other fails; identical test names across packages and parts; an external test package; wrong-file and multiple-match refusals; exact nested subtests containing regexp punctuation and shell-looking text; a proposed-API compile failure followed by real candidate success; and missing-tool, unresolved-dependency, unrelated-package, discovery and interrupted-compilation failures that supply no eligible evidence. Exercise skipped and absent selectors, zero-test success, TestMain exit before m.Run, nonzero abrupt exit, genuine assertion and panic completion, duplicate/stale/conflicting/truncated evidence and fabricated stdout AND stderr lifecycle/JSON/runner records before and during test execution. Verify command policy is preserved or explicitly refused, and no invocation enables network or installation. Use the shared lifecycle's fault injection for transport corruption while retaining real Go fixtures for framework outcomes.

Keep this adapter callable through the lower-level lifecycle for verification, with no candidate-controlled registration and no production admission change yet. The implementation must work in the prepared pinned Go environment without adding Python or relying on a host Go cache. Preserve the built-in unconfigured Go runner, legacy hashes/locks and existing acceptance coverage; this issue does not migrate old plans or infer new ratified metadata. pytest, Vitest and Jest remain explicitly unsupported and external plumbing remains disabled.

Update SPEC.md and docs/factory.md with the implemented adapter API, safe test_one forms, evidence criteria and compiler-versus-setup distinction, accurately retaining the factory admission restriction until integration. Keep README.md accurate and at most 400 lines. Cite existing decision foundations in changed SPEC bullets. The build cannot write decisions/: the merger records the adapter's execution decision before the next issue. Decision recording and unavailable Docker/network checks are Merger work; affected real Python/TLAPS CI suites remain required.

Foundations: D-0105, D-0107, D-0108, D-0110, D-0111, D-0121, D-0122, D-0173, D-0281, D-0282, D-0294, D-0301 and D-0305; #452's ratified plan; #484/D-0311's execution API; #503/D-0314's native identity contract; and the preceding shared-lifecycle issue in #513's ratified plan.

Kind: plumbing

issues.title: Use configured Go evidence in planning and builder checks
issues.body:
Complete #513 by enabling the Go adapter and common lifecycle delivered by the preceding two issues in configured planning and building. This is the final integration of #513 within #501 and step 4 of #452's ratified plan. The lower-level implementation already executes exact captured Go test_one selections and distinguishes framework completion, attributable proposed-API compiler failure and setup failure. Connect it to the factory without weakening the pinned source/identity contract or leaving any required end-to-end work for another issue.

Replace the blanket configured/native refusal in internal/plumbing/check.go and repository_checks.go only for supported native Go acceptance. Check must use the independent base-check path so an expected ordinary suite/test/compile failure cannot stop the individual invocations needed for the rest of the selectors. A draft is proposable only when every acceptance identity has exactly one matching completed eligible failure. An already-passing selector invalidates the draft even when another selector in the same package fails. Skipped, absent, refused, unstarted, running, interrupted, ambiguous or mismatched results cannot qualify; ordinary format/lint/install/launch/setup failures supply no acceptance evidence. Installation, startup, cleanup, deadline and cancellation failures veto qualification even after completed failures.

Sandbox.Run on a candidate must run captured ordinary phases and acceptance through the same configured lifecycle and require all applicable commands and every selector to pass. Keep phase failures separate from individual acceptance outcomes. Neither a successful suite nor Accepted-map fallback nor compiler success alone may produce Passed. Failed final checks cannot lead to review approval or a ready pull request. Preserve the existing second-agent review and at-most-two-repair flow, unchanged ratified plan and acceptance tests, fixed original checkout, fresh final checks and original build allowance.

Use the trusted caller's RepositoryChecks snapshot and verified dependency environment throughout. Before execution reject a changed execution digest, selected identity, or original pinned source; preserve the existing line-ending normalization rule while executing the ratified source bytes. The builder's staging may take only authorized production changes and admitted Go regressions from its workspace; candidate edits cannot replace acceptance sources, selectors, lock, captured configuration or registered authority. Direct configured execution must validate the bytes it will execute, not merely rely on a caller having staged them. A replacement candidate repository.json is never execution authority.

Ensure the separate builder test tool and fresh final checks use the identical registered plan, source, identity, selection and evidence rules through internal/plumbing/checkqueue.go, build.go, stage.go and the tools in cmd/invariant/main.go. Configured planning's queued check tool and final proposal validation must also agree through internal/formalize/plan.go. Retain standalone configured builders' local queue and watcher-owned queues. IPC carries only the registered work identity and workspace/candidate location; it cannot replace policy, adapters or the registered plan. Keep the queue slot until bounded uncanceled cleanup completes, including client disconnect, deadline and cancellation. Tool calls, final checks, fallback and repairs keep the build's existing allowance; within each run all parts, suite and acceptance invocations share the original whole-run deadline and one test-phase allowance without renewal.

Retain full part/framework/file/selector identities, package attribution, completed and unfinished results and reasons in structured outputs and summaries shown to planners and builders. Diagnostic output truncation must not erase or reinterpret them. Say which selector already passed and which did not complete. Keep unsupported pytest, Vitest and Jest explicit and refuse them before dependency preparation; mixed supported/unsupported native plans must not partially qualify. Native execution without captured authority still fails. Legacy-shaped records under a configured sandbox never qualify through suite results or the legacy Accepted fallback: if they lack the pinned execution identity required by this path, refuse them explicitly rather than silently inferring or migrating it. The unconfigured Go runner, all existing Go plan hashes and locks and external-plumbing intake restriction remain unchanged.

Add end-to-end default Go acceptance/regression fixtures without Docker or network, exercising real Go through the production adapter where outcomes matter. Check a real draft on a committed base, retain its exact tests, change only production code, and obtain a genuine candidate pass. Include a passing-plus-failing pair in one package that blocks the proposal, same names in different packages/parts, proposed-API compile failure that qualifies only its attributed selection and becomes a real pass, setup/compiler failures that cannot qualify, and all supported versus unsupported framework paths. Verify a candidate whose ordinary command fails cannot pass despite passing acceptance. Cover source, configuration and selector mismatches before execution, no preparation for unsupported plans, stale evidence across fresh checks, cancellation/deadlines after earlier failure and cleanup errors after otherwise completed evidence.

Include an actual IPC builder fixture with a separate test-tool process. Demonstrate that the tool and fresh final checks execute the same registered acceptance bytes and full identities, agree on genuine outcomes, and both reject forged output and replacement authority. A tool pass must not be reused as final evidence: mutate the allowed production candidate after that call and require the fresh final check to see the change. Cover both standalone and shared-queue registration, failed checks withholding review/ready status, and repairs retaining the original source and authority. Add queued planner coverage showing its check tool and final proposal use the same base verdict. Preserve the pre-existing acceptance suite and its legacy compatibility checks.

Add an opt-in pinned-image Go integration fixture for the completed path: capture a repository contract, prepare a verified environment, run base acceptance failure, make a production-only change, obtain a true candidate pass with unchanged tests, and verify cleanup after success, failure and cancellation. Exercise prepared-environment reuse and offline execution with no check-time installs/downloads, no host cache mount, init and the existing memory/process limits; assert no named container or private staging is left. Normal Go tests stay daemon/network independent. Enabling the opt-in makes missing Docker or failed preparation an error rather than a silent skip. Document its exact command, pinned image/platform prerequisites and expected cleanup.

Update SPEC.md, README.md and docs/factory.md in this issue to describe configured Go acceptance as available: safe test_one forms, independent per-selector completion, base failure versus candidate pass, attributable new-API compilation versus setup failures, shared budgets, cleanup and identical builder/final authority. Keep README.md within 400 lines with detail on its linked factory page. Explicitly state that pytest/Vitest/Jest adapters and external repository intake remain unavailable. Cite the foundations on every changed SPEC bullet. This build cannot write decisions/: the merger records the completed execution decision before #501 proceeds to its next issue. Decision recording and unavailable Docker/network verification belong under Merger work and alone do not require repair; affected opt-in real Python and TLAPS CI suites remain required, not Merger work.

Foundations: D-0105, D-0107, D-0108, D-0110, D-0111, D-0121, D-0122, D-0173, D-0281, D-0282, D-0294, D-0301 and D-0305; #452's ratified plan; #484/D-0311's captured execution API; #503/D-0314's native identity contract; and the two preceding lifecycle and Go-adapter issues in #513's ratified plan. Together these three issues complete #513; no additional adapter, intake or lifecycle follow-up is needed to finish this Go scope.

Kind: plumbing
